title: Practical Counterfactual Policy Learning for Top-K Recommendations

problem.claim: Recommender systems need to learn policies from collected feedback to decide which items to recommend to users.

gap.claim: For top-K policy learning with a large item space, existing approaches face importance weight explosion, observation insufficiency, and training-efficiency difficulties.

contributions.claim: A practical framework is proposed for policy learning in top-K recommendations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed framework.
The authors report that experiments confirm the efficiency of the proposed framework.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems learn recommendation policies from collected user feedback.
Selection bias in collected feedback can produce biased learning and sub-optimal policies.
Counterfactual learning addresses the issue through value-learning or policy-learning approaches.
Top-K policy learning with a large item space has difficulties involving importance weights, observations, and training efficiency.
The work proposes a practical framework and reports effective and efficient experimental results.

source_observation.claim: Selection bias in collected feedback can make learned recommendation policies sub-optimal.

interpretation.claim: Learning from observational feedback requires methods that account for how feedback was selected.

application.claim: Use counterfactual learning approaches when recommendation feedback is affected by selection bias.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when counterfactual learning is unnecessary or which approach is preferable across settings.

source_observation.claim: Top-K policy learning in a large item space involves importance weight explosion, observation insufficiency, and training-efficiency difficulties.

interpretation.claim: Scalable top-K counterfactual policy learning must address statistical and computational constraints together.

application.claim: When designing top-K recommendation policy learners, evaluate importance-weight behavior, observation requirements, and training efficiency jointly.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the framework's assumptions, mechanisms, or applicability beyond the described setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not describe the framework's components or algorithmic details.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, metrics, numerical results, or experimental conditions.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
